title: 1801 Prairie's south pavilion stands nearer its photograph
items: The Kimball house's south pavilion on Prairie Avenue now starts right beside the bowed bay,, as J. W. Taylor's photograph of about 1895 shows. Its stone gable now springs about 0.7 m lower, so the gable, pinnacles and finial meet the photograph's heights. The top-floor pair of windows now sits about 0.8 m higher, close under the band below the gable, as the photograph shows. The pavilion's south corner still stands a little south of the photograph's. That is next: the 1911 map draws the corner cut back at an angle.
